notes.title: Operating Systems (CS3451) • Unit I: Operating System Overview & Process Concepts
notes.subject: Operating Systems

content.shortNotes: Dual-mode CPU operation, System Calls, Process Control Block (PCB), Context Switching, Inter-process Communication (IPC).
content.keyPoints:
• Dual-mode CPU operation protects hardware.
• fork() creates process clones.
• PCB stores CPU register states.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: OS Structure & Dual Mode.
2. 16-Mark: Process State Transition & PCB.
3. 2-Mark: System calls classification.
content.mcqs: 1. Mode bit in kernel mode is: A) 0 [CORRECT] B) 1
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is a context switch? Ans: Saving old PCB state and restoring new PCB state.
content.summary: Foundational OS abstractions, system calls, and PCB management.

notes.title: Operating Systems (CS3451) • Unit II: CPU Scheduling & Process Synchronization
notes.subject: Operating Systems

content.shortNotes: Scheduling criteria (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority), Critical Section Problem (CSP), Peterson's Algorithm, Semaphores, Classic Sync Problems (Producer-Consumer, Dining Philosophers).
content.keyPoints:
• SJF gives minimum average waiting time.
• Peterson's algorithm solves 2-process CSP.
• Semaphores prevent race conditions.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Gantt chart calculations for SJF & Round Robin.
2. 16-Mark: Semaphore implementation of Dining Philosophers.
3. 2-Mark: Define Race Condition.
content.mcqs: 1. Which algorithm gives optimal waiting time? A) SJF [CORRECT] B) FCFS
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Define Semaphore. Ans: An integer variable accessed via atomic wait() and signal() primitives.
content.summary: Scheduling metrics, Peterson's algorithm, and semaphore synchronization.

notes.title: Operating Systems (CS3451) • Unit III: Deadlocks & Memory Management
notes.subject: Operating Systems

content.shortNotes: Coffman Deadlock Conditions, Deadlock Prevention, Banker's Deadlock Avoidance Algorithm, Memory Paging, Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB), Effective Access Time (EAT).
content.keyPoints:
• Banker's algorithm ensures safe states.
• Paging eliminates external fragmentation.
• TLB accelerates address translation.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Banker's safety and resource request numericals.
2. 16-Mark: Paging hardware architecture with TLB.
3. 2-Mark: What is internal fragmentation?
content.mcqs: 1. Banker's algorithm safe state guarantees: A) No deadlock [CORRECT] B) 100% CPU usage
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Thrashing? Ans: High paging activity collapsing CPU utilization.
content.summary: Banker's deadlock avoidance and virtual memory address translation.

notes.title: Operating Systems (CS3451) • Unit IV: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
notes.subject: Operating Systems

content.shortNotes: Demand Paging, Page Fault Trap Handler Sequence, Page Replacement Algorithms (FIFO, Optimal, LRU, Clock), Belady's Anomaly, Working Set Model.
content.keyPoints:
• Demand paging loads pages on demand.
• Belady's anomaly occurs in FIFO.
• Dirty bit avoids unneeded disk writes.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Step-by-step Page Fault Handling routine.
2. 16-Mark: FIFO, Optimal, and LRU numerical comparison.
3. 2-Mark: Define Belady's Anomaly.
content.mcqs: 1. Which algorithm can suffer from Belady's Anomaly? A) FIFO [CORRECT] B) LRU
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Dirty Bit? Ans: Indicates page was modified in RAM since disk load.
content.summary: Demand paging mechanics, page fault cycles, and replacement algorithms.

notes.title: Operating Systems (CS3451) • Unit V: File Systems & Mass Storage Management
notes.subject: Operating Systems

content.shortNotes: File concepts, Directory structures, Disk allocation (Contiguous, Linked, UNIX Inode Indexing), Disk Scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN), RAID levels.
content.keyPoints:
• UNIX Inode uses direct and indirect block pointers.
• C-SCAN provides uniform cylinder wait times.
• RAID 5 provides parity fault tolerance.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: UNIX Inode architecture with direct/indirect blocks.
2. 16-Mark: Disk scheduling calculations for SCAN & C-SCAN.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate Hard vs Soft links.
content.mcqs: 1. Standard direct block pointers in UNIX Inode: A) 12 [CORRECT] B) 8
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Differentiate Hard vs Soft link. Ans: Hard link points to inode; Soft link stores target path.
content.summary: File systems, UNIX Inode indexing, and elevator disk head scheduling.

notes.title: Database Management Systems (CS3391) • Unit I: Relational Databases & SQL Fundamentals
notes.subject: Database Management Systems

content.shortNotes: 3-Schema Architecture, Data Independence, ER Modeling, Relational Algebra (Selection, Projection, Join, Cartesian Product), DDL/DML SQL.
content.keyPoints:
• Physical and Logical data independence.
• Primary keys uniquely identify rows.
• Relational algebra provides mathematical SQL foundation.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: 3-tier ANSI-SPARC Architecture.
2. 16-Mark: ER Diagram reduction to tables.
3. 2-Mark: Define Candidate Key.
content.mcqs: 1. Relational algebra row filter: A) Selection ($\sigma$) [CORRECT] B) Projection ($\pi$)
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Differentiate DDL and DML. Ans: DDL defines schemas; DML manages data records.
content.summary: 3-tier database architecture, ER modeling, and Relational Algebra.

notes.title: Database Management Systems (CS3391) • Unit II: Advanced SQL & Database Normalization
notes.subject: Database Management Systems

content.shortNotes: Functional Dependencies, Armstrong's Axioms, 1NF, 2NF (No partial dependency), 3NF (No transitive dependency), BCNF (Strict superkey LHS), Lossless Decomposition.
content.keyPoints:
• Normalization eliminates insert/update/delete anomalies.
• BCNF is stricter than 3NF.
• Lossless join ensures zero data loss upon reconstruction.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Step-by-step Normalization from 1NF to BCNF.
2. 16-Mark: Attribute closure algorithm.
3. 2-Mark: State BCNF condition.
content.mcqs: 1. In BCNF, LHS of non-trivial $X \to Y$ must be: A) Super Key [CORRECT] B) Foreign Key
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Transitive Dependency? Ans: When non-prime attribute determines another non-prime attribute.
content.summary: Functional dependencies and lossless decomposition up to BCNF.

notes.title: Database Management Systems (CS3391) • Unit III: Transactions & Concurrency Control
notes.subject: Database Management Systems

content.shortNotes: ACID Properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability), Serializability, Precedence Graph, Two-Phase Locking (2PL, Strict 2PL), Write-Ahead Logging (WAL).
content.keyPoints:
• ACID ensures transaction reliability.
• Conflict serializability tested via cycle graphs.
• Strict 2PL prevents cascading rollbacks.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Precedence graph conflict serializability testing.
2. 16-Mark: Two-Phase Locking protocol.
3. 2-Mark: State ACID properties.
content.mcqs: 1. Property ensuring committed data survives crashes: A) Durability [CORRECT] B) Atomicity
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Differentiate Shared vs Exclusive lock. Ans: Shared allows reads; Exclusive allows writes.
content.summary: ACID transaction semantics, 2PL locking, and WAL recovery.

notes.title: Database Management Systems (CS3391) • Unit IV: Query Processing & Indexing Techniques
notes.subject: Database Management Systems

content.shortNotes: Query Processing Pipeline, Query Tree Optimization Heuristics, Cost Estimation, B-Trees & B+ Tree Indexing (all data in linked leaves, balanced height).
content.keyPoints:
• B+ Trees minimize disk seeks with wide fanout.
• Clustered index defines physical disk row ordering.
• Optimizer selects optimal join order using cost statistics.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Structure, search, insertion in B+ Tree.
2. 16-Mark: Query tree heuristic optimization.
3. 2-Mark: Why B+ Tree over B Tree?
content.mcqs: 1. In B+ Tree, data records reside in: A) Leaf Nodes [CORRECT] B) Root
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Why are B+ Tree range queries fast? Ans: Leaf nodes are linked in a continuous doubly linked list.
content.summary: Query optimization heuristics and B+ Tree indexing architectures.

notes.title: Database Management Systems (CS3391) • Unit V: Distributed Databases & NoSQL Systems
notes.subject: Database Management Systems

content.shortNotes: Distributed DBMS, Two-Phase Commit (2PC), CAP Theorem (Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance), NoSQL Types (Document, Key-Value, Columnar, Graph).
content.keyPoints:
• CAP theorem limits simultaneous guarantees to 2 of 3.
• 2PC ensures distributed transaction atomicity.
• NoSQL provides horizontal sharding and flexible schemas.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: CAP Theorem trade-offs.
2. 16-Mark: NoSQL Database classification & comparison.
3. 2-Mark: Explain Two-Phase Commit.
content.mcqs: 1. Theorem proving C, A, P cannot all hold: A) CAP Theorem [CORRECT] B) Amdahl's Law
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Eventual Consistency? Ans: Replicas eventually converge to identical latest values.
content.summary: Distributed databases, 2PC protocol, and NoSQL systems.

notes.title: Computer Networks (CS3591) • Unit I: Physical Layer & Network Models
notes.subject: Computer Networks

content.shortNotes: OSI 7-Layer Model, TCP/IP Protocol Suite, Transmission Media, Guided & Unguided Media, Switching (Circuit, Packet, Message Switching).
content.keyPoints:
• OSI defines 7 conceptual layers; TCP/IP has 4 operational layers.
• Packet switching uses statistical multiplexing.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: OSI vs TCP/IP layered architecture.
2. 16-Mark: Circuit vs Packet switching comparison.
3. 2-Mark: Name layers of OSI model.
content.mcqs: 1. Layer responsible for hop-to-hop node delivery: A) Data Link Layer [CORRECT] B) Transport
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Differentiate Circuit vs Packet switching. Ans: Circuit establishes dedicated path; Packet breaks data into independent datagrams.
content.summary: OSI/TCP-IP reference models and data transmission fundamentals.

notes.title: Computer Networks (CS3591) • Unit II: Data Link Layer & Medium Access
notes.subject: Computer Networks

content.shortNotes: Framing, Error Detection (CRC Polynomial Division, Checksum), Sliding Window Protocols (Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat), CSMA/CD & CSMA/CA, Ethernet IEEE 802.3.
content.keyPoints:
• CRC detects burst errors with polynomial division.
• Selective Repeat retransmits only corrupted frames.
• CSMA/CD halts and jams on collision in wired Ethernet.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: CRC error detection numerical problem.
2. 16-Mark: Sliding window Go-Back-N vs Selective Repeat.
3. 2-Mark: What is binary exponential backoff?
content.mcqs: 1. Protocol that retransmits only damaged frames: A) Selective Repeat [CORRECT] B) Go-Back-N
content.vivaQuestions: Q: How does CSMA/CD detect collisions? Ans: Nodes monitor voltage levels during transmission.
content.summary: Data Link framing, CRC error detection, and MAC protocols.

notes.title: Computer Networks (CS3591) • Unit III: Network Layer & IP Routing
notes.subject: Computer Networks

content.shortNotes: IPv4 Addressing & CIDR Subnetting, IPv6 Header, Routing Protocols (Distance Vector / RIP with Count-to-Infinity, Link State / OSPF with Dijkstra's Shortest Path, BGP), ARP & ICMP.
content.keyPoints:
• Subnetting divides IP blocks into broadcast domains.
• OSPF floods link-state packets to calculate shortest paths.
• ARP resolves 32-bit IP address to 48-bit MAC address.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: IPv4 Subnetting & CIDR numerical problems.
2. 16-Mark: Dijkstra's shortest path routing algorithm.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate IPv4 vs IPv6 headers.
content.mcqs: 1. Routing protocol using Dijkstra algorithm: A) OSPF [CORRECT] B) RIP
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Count-to-Infinity in RIP? Ans: Routing loop where distance estimates increment indefinitely.
content.summary: IPv4/IPv6 addressing, CIDR subnetting, and OSPF/BGP routing.

notes.title: Computer Networks (CS3591) • Unit IV: Transport Layer Protocols
notes.subject: Computer Networks

content.shortNotes: UDP (Connectionless, Unreliable, Fast), TCP (Connection-Oriented, 3-Way Handshake SYN/ACK, Flow Control with Sliding Window, Congestion Control: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, Fast Recovery).
content.keyPoints:
• TCP 3-way handshake establishes bidirectional sync.
• TCP Congestion Control adjusts congestion window (cwnd).
• UDP avoids connection overhead for real-time video/DNS.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: TCP 3-way handshake connection establishment & teardown.
2. 16-Mark: TCP Congestion Control algorithms (AIMD, Slow Start).
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate TCP vs UDP.
content.mcqs: 1. TCP Connection establishment uses: A) 3-Way Handshake [CORRECT] B) 2-Way Ping
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Silly Window Syndrome? Ans: Inefficient transmission of tiny data payloads.
content.summary: Transport layer end-to-end reliability, TCP 3-way handshake, and congestion control.

notes.title: Computer Networks (CS3591) • Unit V: Application Layer & Network Security
notes.subject: Computer Networks

content.shortNotes: DNS (Domain Name System resolution), HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3, SMTP/POP3/IMAP Email, Cryptography (Symmetric AES, Asymmetric RSA, Digital Signatures, SSL/TLS Handshake, Firewalls).
content.keyPoints:
• DNS translates hostnames to IP addresses recursively.
• RSA uses public encryption key and private decryption key.
• TLS provides transport-level confidentiality and authentication.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: DNS hierarchy and recursive/iterative query resolution.
2. 16-Mark: RSA public-key cryptographic algorithm numerical calculation.
3. 2-Mark: How does SSL/TLS handshake secure HTTP?
content.mcqs: 1. Asymmetric cryptographic algorithm based on prime factorization: A) RSA [CORRECT] B) AES
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is the difference between Symmetric and Asymmetric encryption? Ans: Symmetric uses 1 shared secret; Asymmetric uses public-private key pair.
content.summary: Application layer protocols (DNS, HTTP) and TLS/RSA network security.

notes.title: Machine Learning (AD3501) • Unit I: Introduction & Supervised Linear Models
notes.subject: Machine Learning

content.shortNotes: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning, Linear Regression, Gradient Descent, Normal Equation, Logistic Regression, Cost Functions, Regularization (L1 Lasso, L2 Ridge).
content.keyPoints:
• Gradient descent iteratively minimizes mean squared error.
• L1 Lasso enforces sparsity; L2 Ridge penalizes large weights.
• Logistic regression models class probability via Sigmoid function.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Linear regression derivation using Gradient Descent.
2. 16-Mark: Logistic Regression cost function and decision boundary.
3. 2-Mark: Compare L1 Lasso vs L2 Ridge regularization.
content.mcqs: 1. Sigmoid function maps real values to: A) (0, 1) [CORRECT] B) (-1, 1)
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is the Bias-Variance Tradeoff? Ans: Underfitting has high bias; Overfitting has high variance.
content.summary: Linear/logistic regression, gradient descent optimization, and regularization.

notes.title: Machine Learning (AD3501) • Unit II: Decision Trees & Support Vector Machines
notes.subject: Machine Learning

content.shortNotes: Decision Trees (ID3, C4.5, CART), Entropy, Information Gain, Gini Impurity, Pruning, Support Vector Machines (Max Margin, Soft Margin $C$, Kernel Trick: RBF, Polynomial).
content.keyPoints:
• Information Gain measures entropy reduction after split.
• SVM maximizes margin $\frac{2}{||w||}$ between support vectors.
• Kernel trick evaluates dot products in high-dimensional space.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Decision tree induction numerical with Information Gain.
2. 16-Mark: Support Vector Machine dual formulation and kernel functions.
3. 2-Mark: Define Gini Impurity.
content.mcqs: 1. In SVM, vectors defining the decision hyperplane are: A) Support Vectors [CORRECT] B) Centroids
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Tree Pruning? Ans: Removing tree branches that provide little predictive power to reduce overfitting.
content.summary: Decision tree splitting metrics, SVM maximum margin, and kernel methods.

notes.title: Machine Learning (AD3501) • Unit III: Ensemble Methods & Clustering
notes.subject: Machine Learning

content.shortNotes: Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregation, Random Forests), Boosting (AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost), Unsupervised K-Means Clustering, Elbow Method, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering, DBSCAN.
content.keyPoints:
• Random Forest reduces variance via decorrelated trees.
• Boosting iteratively fits models to residuals to reduce bias.
• DBSCAN discovers arbitrarily shaped clusters based on density.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: AdaBoost weight update and classifier combination.
2. 16-Mark: K-Means clustering step-by-step numerical calculation.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate Bagging vs Boosting.
content.mcqs: 1. Random Forest primarily reduces: A) Variance [CORRECT] B) Bias
content.vivaQuestions: Q: How is optimal $k$ chosen in K-Means? Ans: Using the Elbow method on Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WCSS).
content.summary: Ensemble algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost) and clustering techniques (K-Means, DBSCAN).

notes.title: Machine Learning (AD3501) • Unit IV: Probabilistic Models & Dimensionality Reduction
notes.subject: Machine Learning

content.shortNotes: Bayes' Theorem, Naive Bayes Classifier (Laplace Smoothing), Expectation-Maximization (EM) Algorithm, Principal Component Analysis (PCA, Covariance Matrix, Eigenvectors), t-SNE.
content.keyPoints:
• Naive Bayes assumes conditional independence among features.
• PCA projects data onto orthogonal directions of maximum variance.
• Laplace smoothing prevents zero-frequency multiplication collapse.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Naive Bayes text classification numerical with Laplace smoothing.
2. 16-Mark: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) step-by-step mathematical derivation.
3. 2-Mark: State Bayes' Theorem.
content.mcqs: 1. PCA selects principal directions based on: A) Maximum variance [CORRECT] B) Minimum mean
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Why is Laplace smoothing used in Naive Bayes? Ans: To prevent zero probability for unseen words.
content.summary: Probabilistic Naive Bayes classification and PCA dimensionality reduction.

notes.title: Machine Learning (AD3501) • Unit V: Model Evaluation, Neural Nets & Ethics
notes.subject: Machine Learning

content.shortNotes: Confusion Matrix (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC), K-Fold Cross Validation, Artificial Neural Networks (Perceptron, Multilayer Perceptron, Backpropagation), AI Ethics, Bias & Fairness.
content.keyPoints:
• Precision measures exactness; Recall measures completeness.
• Backpropagation applies chain rule of calculus to update weights.
• AI ethics requires mitigating algorithmic bias and ensuring explainability.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Multilayer Perceptron Backpropagation weight update derivation.
2. 16-Mark: Model evaluation metrics (Precision, Recall, ROC-AUC) numerical.
3. 2-Mark: Define F1-Score.
content.mcqs: 1. Harmonic mean of Precision and Recall is: A) F1-Score [CORRECT] B) Accuracy
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Backpropagation? Ans: Backward propagation of output errors using chain rule to calculate weight gradients.
content.summary: Model validation metrics, backpropagation neural networks, and AI ethics.

notes.title: Electronic Devices & Circuits (EC3351) • Unit I: Semiconductor Diodes & Special Diodes
notes.subject: Electronic Devices & Circuits

content.shortNotes: PN Junction Diode, Depletion Region, Diode Current Equation, V-I Characteristics, Breakdown (Zener vs Avalanche), Zener Voltage Regulator, Tunnel Diode, Varactor Diode, Photodiode, Solar Cell.
content.keyPoints:
• Zener breakdown occurs in heavily doped diodes at low reverse voltages.
• Zener diode operates in reverse breakdown as constant voltage reference.
• Solar cell generates EMF via photovoltaic effect.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: PN junction diode operation in forward and reverse bias with energy band diagrams.
2. 16-Mark: Zener diode as voltage regulator with line and load regulation calculations.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate Zener vs Avalanche breakdown.
content.mcqs: 1. Diode operating in reverse breakdown for voltage regulation: A) Zener Diode [CORRECT] B) LED
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Barrier Potential? Ans: Built-in potential across PN junction preventing further majority carrier diffusion.
content.summary: Semiconductor PN junction physics, Zener voltage regulators, and optoelectronic diodes.

notes.title: Electronic Devices & Circuits (EC3351) • Unit II: BJT & Small Signal Amplifiers
notes.subject: Electronic Devices & Circuits

content.shortNotes: Bipolar Junction Transistor (CB, CE, CC configurations), Input/Output Characteristics, Transistor Biasing (Fixed Bias, Voltage Divider Bias, Stability Factors), Small-Signal Hybrid-$\pi$ Model, CE Amplifier Frequency Response.
content.keyPoints:
• Voltage divider bias provides best Q-point thermal stability.
• CE amplifier provides high voltage and current gain with $180^\circ$ phase shift.
• Hybrid-pi model represents transistor as transconductance source.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Voltage Divider Biasing circuit analysis and stability factor $S$ derivation.
2. 16-Mark: Common-Emitter small signal hybrid-pi equivalent circuit and voltage gain derivation.
3. 2-Mark: What is thermal runaway in BJT?
content.mcqs: 1. Transistor configuration providing both voltage and current gain: A) Common Emitter (CE) [CORRECT] B) Common Base (CB)
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Thermal Runaway? Ans: Uncontrolled $I_C$ increase with temperature leading to transistor destruction.
content.summary: BJT configurations, voltage divider biasing stability, and small-signal amplifiers.

notes.title: Electronic Devices & Circuits (EC3351) • Unit III: FET & MOSFET Amplifiers
notes.subject: Electronic Devices & Circuits

content.shortNotes: JFET Construction and Characteristics, Depletion and Enhancement MOSFET, Drain and Transfer Characteristics, Small Signal MOSFET Model, Common Source (CS) Amplifier, High-Frequency Response & Miller Effect.
content.keyPoints:
• MOSFET is voltage-controlled with near-infinite gate input resistance.
• In saturation, MOSFET acts as constant current source.
• Miller effect multiplies feedback capacitance, reducing high-frequency bandwidth.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Enhancement MOSFET construction, operation, and drain/transfer characteristics.
2. 16-Mark: Small signal analysis of Common Source (CS) MOSFET amplifier.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate JFET vs MOSFET.
content.mcqs: 1. MOSFET parameter that relates drain current change to gate voltage change: A) Transconductance ($g_m$) [CORRECT] B) Dynamic resistance
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Pinch-Off Voltage in JFET? Ans: Minimum $V_{DS}$ where depletion regions touch and drain current saturates.
content.summary: JFET and MOSFET characteristics, CS amplifiers, and Miller effect bandwidth bounds.

notes.title: Electronic Devices & Circuits (EC3351) • Unit IV: Differential & Multistage Amplifiers
notes.subject: Electronic Devices & Circuits

content.shortNotes: Differential Amplifier (BJT & MOSFET), Common-Mode and Differential-Mode Operation, CMRR (Common Mode Rejection Ratio), Multistage Amplifiers (Cascade, Cascode, Darlington Pair), Power Amplifiers (Class A, Class B Push-Pull, Class AB, Class C).
content.keyPoints:
• Differential amplifier amplifies difference signal while rejecting common-mode noise.
• High CMRR indicates superior common-mode noise suppression.
• Class B Push-Pull achieves up to 78.5% efficiency but suffers from crossover distortion.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: BJT Differential Amplifier analysis for differential and common mode gains, CMRR derivation.
2. 16-Mark: Class B Push-Pull Power Amplifier efficiency and crossover distortion.
3. 2-Mark: Define CMRR.
content.mcqs: 1. Maximum theoretical efficiency of Class B Push-Pull amplifier: A) 78.5% [CORRECT] B) 25% C) 50%
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What causes Crossover Distortion? Ans: Transistors turning off when input voltage falls below barrier potential (0.7V).
content.summary: Differential amplifiers, CMRR analysis, Darlington pairs, and Class A/B power stages.

notes.title: Electronic Devices & Circuits (EC3351) • Unit V: Feedback Amplifiers & Oscillators
notes.subject: Electronic Devices & Circuits

content.shortNotes: Feedback Concepts, Types of Feedback (Voltage-Series, Voltage-Shunt, Current-Series, Current-Shunt), Effects of Negative Feedback, Barkhausen Criterion for Oscillation, RC Phase Shift Oscillator, Wien Bridge Oscillator, Hartley, Colpitts, Crystal Oscillators.
content.keyPoints:
• Negative feedback increases bandwidth, stabilizes gain, and reduces distortion.
• Barkhausen criterion: Loop gain $|A\beta| = 1$ and phase shift $= 0^\circ$ or $360^\circ$.
• Crystal oscillators provide exceptional frequency stability via piezoelectric effect.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Effects of negative feedback on gain, input/output resistance, bandwidth, and noise.
2. 16-Mark: RC Phase Shift Oscillator frequency derivation with BJT/FET circuit.
3. 2-Mark: State Barkhausen Criterion for oscillation.
content.mcqs: 1. Barkhausen criterion requires loop gain $|A\beta|$ equal to: A) 1 [CORRECT] B) 0 C) Infinity
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Why are Crystal Oscillators highly stable? Ans: Quartz crystals possess high mechanical quality factor $Q$ and low temperature coefficient.
content.summary: Negative feedback topologies, Barkhausen criterion, and sinusoidal oscillators.

notes.title: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE3251) • Unit I: DC Circuit Analysis & Network Theorems
notes.subject: Electric Circuit Analysis

content.shortNotes: Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's Laws (KCL, KVL), Mesh Current and Node Voltage Methods, Thevenin's Theorem, Norton's Theorem, Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, Superposition Theorem, Star-Delta Transformations.
content.keyPoints:
• KCL is conservation of charge; KVL is conservation of energy.
• Thevenin replaces linear network with $V_{th}$ in series with $R_{th}$.
• Max power transferred when load resistance equals Thevenin resistance ($R_L = R_{th}$).
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Thevenin and Norton equivalent circuit numerical problem.
2. 16-Mark: Maximum Power Transfer theorem proof for DC and AC networks.
3. 2-Mark: State Kirchhoff's Current Law and Voltage Law.
content.mcqs: 1. Maximum power is transferred to load when $R_L$ equals: A) $R_{th}$ [CORRECT] B) 0 C) Infinity
content.vivaQuestions: Q: State Superposition Theorem. Ans: In a linear bilateral network with multiple sources, response is the algebraic sum of responses caused by each independent source acting alone.
content.summary: Mesh/nodal analysis, Thevenin/Norton equivalents, and Maximum Power Transfer theorem.

notes.title: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE3251) • Unit II: AC Circuit Analysis & Resonance
notes.subject: Electric Circuit Analysis

content.shortNotes: Sinusoidal AC Waveforms, Phasor Representation, RMS and Average Values, Form Factor, Peak Factor, RLC Series and Parallel Circuits, Series Resonance (Resonant Frequency $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, Quality Factor $Q$, Bandwidth), Parallel Resonance (Anti-resonance).
content.keyPoints:
• Phasors represent sinusoidal steady-state voltages and currents as rotating vectors.
• At series resonance, impedance is purely resistive and minimum ($Z = R$), current is maximum.
• Quality factor $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C R}$ measures selectivity.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Series RLC resonant circuit derivation for $f_0$, Quality factor $Q$, and Bandwidth.
2. 16-Mark: Phasor analysis of series-parallel RLC circuit with power factor calculation.
3. 2-Mark: Define Quality Factor ($Q$) of a resonant circuit.
content.mcqs: 1. At series resonance in an RLC circuit, the circuit impedance is: A) Purely Resistive and Minimum [CORRECT] B) Maximum
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Power Factor? Ans: Cosine of the phase angle between voltage and current ($\cos\phi = P/S$).
content.summary: Sinusoidal steady-state AC, phasor diagrams, and RLC resonant circuits.

notes.title: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE3251) • Unit III: Transient Analysis & Laplace Transforms
notes.subject: Electric Circuit Analysis

content.shortNotes: First Order RL and RC Circuits (Step and Natural Response), Second Order RLC Circuits (Overdamped, Critically Damped, Underdamped Responses), Transient Analysis using Laplace Transforms, Initial and Final Value Theorems.
content.keyPoints:
• Time constant $\tau = L/R$ for RL circuits; $\tau = RC$ for RC circuits.
• System reaches 63.2% steady state at $t = \tau$, and ~99.3% at $t = 5\tau$.
• Laplace transforms convert differential equations into algebraic equations in the $s$-domain.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Step response transient derivation of series RL and RC circuits with differential equations.
2. 16-Mark: Transient analysis of series RLC circuit for underdamped and critically damped conditions.
3. 2-Mark: State the time constant of series RL and RC circuits.
content.mcqs: 1. Time constant $\tau$ of a series RC circuit is: A) $RC$ [CORRECT] B) $R/C$ C) $1/(RC)$
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is the physical significance of time constant? Ans: Time taken for response to reach 63.2% of its final steady-state value.
content.summary: First/second order circuit transient responses and Laplace transform methods.

notes.title: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE3251) • Unit IV: Coupled Circuits & Polyphase Systems
notes.subject: Electric Circuit Analysis

content.shortNotes: Mutual Inductance ($M$), Self Inductance ($L_1, L_2$), Coefficient of Coupling ($k = \frac{M}{\sqrt{L_1 L_2}}$), Dot Convention, Ideal Transformer, Three-Phase Systems (Star and Delta Connections), Line and Phase Voltages/Currents, Two-Wattmeter Power Measurement.
content.keyPoints:
• Dot convention indicates relative polarity of mutually induced voltages.
• In Star: $V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}, I_L = I_{ph}$. In Delta: $V_L = V_{ph}, I_L = \sqrt{3} I_{ph}$.
• Total 3-phase power $P = \sqrt{3} V_L I_L \cos\phi = W_1 + W_2$.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Two-Wattmeter method for balanced three-phase power and power factor measurement.
2. 16-Mark: Coupled coil analysis in series-aiding and series-opposing configurations.
3. 2-Mark: State the relation between line and phase values in Star and Delta systems.
content.mcqs: 1. Relation between Line and Phase Voltage in a balanced Star-connected 3-phase system: A) $V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}$ [CORRECT] B) $V_L = V_{ph}$
content.vivaQuestions: Q: Why is Three-Phase power preferred over Single-Phase? Ans: Constant instantaneous power, higher transmission efficiency, smaller conductor size, and self-starting motors.
content.summary: Magnetic coupling, dot convention, 3-phase star/delta systems, and two-wattmeter method.

notes.title: Electric Circuit Analysis (EE3251) • Unit V: Two-Port Networks & Duality
notes.subject: Electric Circuit Analysis

content.shortNotes: Two-Port Network Parameters: $Z$-parameters (Impedance), $Y$-parameters (Admittance), $h$-parameters (Hybrid), $ABCD$-parameters (Transmission), Parameter Interconversions, Symmetrical and Reciprocal Network Conditions, Interconnection of Two-Port Networks, Network Duality.
content.keyPoints:
• Reciprocity condition: $Z_{12} = Z_{21}, Y_{12} = Y_{21}, AD - BC = 1, h_{12} = -h_{21}$.
• Symmetry condition: $Z_{11} = Z_{22}, Y_{11} = Y_{22}, A = D, \Delta h = 1$.
• Cascaded two-port networks multiply their transmission $ABCD$ matrices.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Derivation and interconversion between $Z, Y, ABCD,$ and $h$ parameters for a T and $\Pi$ network.
2. 16-Mark: Condition for reciprocity and symmetry for all two-port network parameters.
3. 2-Mark: State the reciprocity condition in terms of $ABCD$ parameters.
content.mcqs: 1. Condition for reciprocity in $ABCD$ transmission parameters is: A) $AD - BC = 1$ [CORRECT] B) $A = D$
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is a Dual Network? Ans: A circuit whose mesh equations have the exact mathematical form of another circuit's nodal equations.
content.summary: Two-port network parameters ($Z, Y, h, ABCD$), reciprocity conditions, and duality.

notes.title: Engineering Thermodynamics (ME3351) • Unit I: Basic Concepts & First Law of Thermodynamics
notes.subject: Engineering Thermodynamics

content.shortNotes: Thermodynamic Systems (Open, Closed, Isolated), Properties (Intensive vs Extensive), Zeroth Law & Temperature Scales, First Law for Closed System ($Q - W = \Delta U$), Flow Work and Steady Flow Energy Equation (SFEE) for Nozzles, Turbines, Compressors, Throttling.
content.keyPoints:
• Zeroth law provides basis for temperature measurement.
• First law is conservation of energy; internal energy is a point function.
• SFEE: $h_1 + \frac{C_1^2}{2000} + \frac{g z_1}{1000} + q = h_2 + \frac{C_2^2}{2000} + \frac{g z_2}{1000} + w$.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Steady Flow Energy Equation (SFEE) derivation and application to Steam Nozzle and Turbine.
2. 16-Mark: First Law non-flow process calculations for Isobaric, Isothermal, Polytropic ($PV^n=C$) processes.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate Intensive vs Extensive thermodynamic properties.
content.mcqs: 1. First Law of Thermodynamics is the law of conservation of: A) Energy [CORRECT] B) Mass C) Momentum
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is a Quasi-Static Process? Ans: An idealized process carried out infinitely slowly such that the system remains in thermodynamic equilibrium at every instant.
content.summary: Zeroth/First Laws, non-flow thermodynamic processes, and SFEE energy balance.

notes.title: Engineering Thermodynamics (ME3351) • Unit II: Second Law & Entropy Analysis
notes.subject: Engineering Thermodynamics

content.shortNotes: Second Law Statements (Kelvin-Planck, Clausius), Reversible vs Irreversible Processes, Carnot Cycle and Theorems, Clausius Inequality ($\oint \delta Q/T \le 0$), Concept of Entropy ($dS = \delta Q/T$), Principle of Increase of Entropy, Available Energy, Exergy, Irreversibility ($I = T_0 S_{gen}$).
content.keyPoints:
• Kelvin-Planck denies 100% heat-to-work conversion from single thermal reservoir.
• Carnot efficiency $\eta = 1 - T_L/T_H$ is highest possible between given thermal limits.
• Total entropy of isolated universe always increases in irreversible processes.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Carnot cycle on P-V and T-s diagrams with efficiency derivation.
2. 16-Mark: Clausius theorem proof, definition of entropy, and entropy generation calculations.
3. 2-Mark: State Kelvin-Planck statement of Second Law.
content.mcqs: 1. Maximum possible efficiency of a heat engine between 600 K and 300 K: A) 50% [CORRECT] B) 100% C) 25%
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Clausius Inequality? Ans: $\oint \delta Q/T \le 0$, equal to zero for reversible cycles and negative for irreversible cycles.
content.summary: Second Law statements, Carnot efficiency limits, Clausius theorem, and entropy.

notes.title: Engineering Thermodynamics (ME3351) • Unit III: Properties of Pure Substances & Steam Power Cycles
notes.subject: Engineering Thermodynamics

content.shortNotes: Pure Substances, Phase Transformation on P-v, T-s, and h-s (Mollier) Diagrams, Triple Point, Critical Point, Dryness Fraction ($x$), Steam Tables, Rankine Cycle with Reheat and Regeneration, Cycle Efficiency Optimization.
content.keyPoints:
• Critical point of water: $P_c = 22.064\text{ MPa}, T_c = 373.95^\circ\text{C}$.
• Rankine cycle is the ideal thermodynamic cycle for steam turbine power plants.
• Reheating increases steam quality at turbine exhaust, preventing blade erosion.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Rankine cycle with superheated steam analysis on T-s and h-s diagrams with reheat efficiency calculations.
2. 16-Mark: Pure substance phase change on P-v-T surface and Mollier diagram usage.
3. 2-Mark: Define Dryness Fraction of steam.
content.mcqs: 1. The ideal thermodynamic cycle for steam thermal power plants is: A) Rankine Cycle [CORRECT] B) Otto Cycle
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is the Critical Point of a substance? Ans: State at which liquid and vapor phases are indistinguishable, with zero latent heat of vaporization.
content.summary: Pure substance thermodynamics, Mollier diagrams, and Reheat/Regenerative Rankine cycles.

notes.title: Engineering Thermodynamics (ME3351) • Unit IV: Ideal & Real Gas Mixtures and Psychrometry
notes.subject: Engineering Thermodynamics

content.shortNotes: Ideal Gas Equation of State ($PV = mRT$), Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures, Amagat's Law, Real Gas van der Waals Equation ($(P + a/v^2)(v - b) = RT$), Compressibility Chart, Psychrometric Properties (Dry Bulb, Wet Bulb, Dew Point Temperatures, Relative Humidity), Psychrometric Chart Processes.
content.keyPoints:
• Dalton's law: Total pressure of non-reacting gas mixture equals sum of partial pressures.
• van der Waals equation accounts for molecular volume ($b$) and intermolecular attraction ($a$).
• Psychrometry analyzes moist air thermodynamic properties in HVAC design.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Derivation of apparent molecular weight and gas constant for ideal gas mixtures.
2. 16-Mark: Psychrometric chart analysis for Sensible Heating, Cooling with Dehumidification, and Evaporative Cooling.
3. 2-Mark: Define Relative Humidity and Specific Humidity.
content.mcqs: 1. In moist air, the temperature at which condensation begins when cooled at constant pressure is: A) Dew Point Temperature [CORRECT] B) Wet Bulb
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Compressibility Factor $Z$? Ans: $Z = PV/(RT)$, measuring the deviation of real gas behavior from ideal gas laws ($Z=1$).
content.summary: Gas mixtures, van der Waals real gas equation, and psychrometric HVAC processes.

notes.title: Engineering Thermodynamics (ME3351) • Unit V: Gas Power Cycles & IC Engines
notes.subject: Engineering Thermodynamics

content.shortNotes: Air Standard Cycles: Otto Cycle (Spark Ignition), Diesel Cycle (Compression Ignition), Dual Combustion Cycle, Brayton Cycle (Gas Turbines), Mean Effective Pressure (MEP), Comparison of Otto, Diesel, and Dual Cycles for Same Compression Ratio and Heat Input.
content.keyPoints:
• Otto cycle uses constant volume heat addition; Diesel uses constant pressure heat addition.
• For same compression ratio, $\eta_{Otto} > \eta_{Dual} > \eta_{Diesel}$.
• Brayton cycle powers jet propulsion and industrial gas turbines with constant pressure combustion.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Air-standard efficiency derivation of Otto Cycle and Diesel Cycle with P-V and T-s diagrams.
2. 16-Mark: Brayton cycle efficiency and maximum work output temperature ratio derivation.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate Otto Cycle and Diesel Cycle.
content.mcqs: 1. Thermal efficiency of an Otto cycle depends directly on: A) Compression Ratio ($r$) and specific heat ratio ($\gamma$) [CORRECT] B) Cylinder weight
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Cut-off Ratio in Diesel Cycle? Ans: Ratio of cylinder volume after fuel injection to volume before fuel injection ($r_c = V_3/V_2$).
content.summary: Air standard power cycles (Otto, Diesel, Dual, Brayton) and IC engine thermodynamics.

notes.title: Structural Analysis (CE3501) • Unit I: Strain Energy & Deflection Methods
notes.subject: Structural Analysis

content.shortNotes: Strain Energy in Axial, Bending, Shear, and Torsion, Castigliano's First and Second Theorems, Principle of Virtual Work (Unit Load Method), Deflection of Statically Determinate Trusses and Beams, Maxwell's Reciprocal Theorem, Betti's Law.
content.keyPoints:
• Castigliano's 2nd theorem: Deflection $\delta_i = \frac{\partial U}{\partial P_i}$.
• Unit load method computes displacements by integrating virtual internal bending moments.
• Maxwell's reciprocal theorem establishes deflection symmetry across load points.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Castigliano's theorem derivation and application to find deflection in pin-jointed trusses.
2. 16-Mark: Unit Load Method for deflection calculation of cantilever and simply supported beams.
3. 2-Mark: State Castigliano's First and Second Theorems.
content.mcqs: 1. Partial derivative of total strain energy with respect to a concentrated load gives: A) Deflection at that point [CORRECT] B) Slope C) Bending moment
content.vivaQuestions: Q: State Maxwell's Reciprocal Theorem. Ans: In a linear elastic structure, deflection at point A due to unit load at B equals deflection at B due to unit load at A.
content.summary: Strain energy principles, Castigliano's deflection theorems, and Unit Load Method.

notes.title: Structural Analysis (CE3501) • Unit II: Slope Deflection Method
notes.subject: Structural Analysis

content.shortNotes: Kinematic Indeterminacy, Slope Deflection Equations for Beams with and without Support Settlement, Analysis of Continuous Beams, Analysis of Rigid Portal Frames (Non-Sway and Sway Analysis), Construction of Shear Force and Bending Moment Diagrams.
content.keyPoints:
• Slope deflection relates end moments to joint rotations ($\theta$) and settlements ($\Delta$).
• Equation: $M_{AB} = M_{FAB} + \frac{2EI}{L}[2\theta_A + \theta_B - \frac{3\Delta}{L}]$.
• Equilibrium equations at joints satisfy $\sum M = 0$.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Analysis of continuous beam with support sinking using Slope Deflection Method.
2. 16-Mark: Portal frame sway analysis using Slope Deflection equations with shear equation.
3. 2-Mark: Write the basic Slope Deflection equation for member AB.
content.mcqs: 1. Number of equilibrium equations required in Slope Deflection method equals the structure's: A) Kinematic Indeterminacy [CORRECT] B) Static Indeterminacy
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Sway in portal frames? Ans: Lateral deflection of frame columns caused by unsymmetrical loading, unequal column heights, or lateral wind/seismic loads.
content.summary: Slope Deflection equations, continuous beam analysis, and portal frame sway mechanics.

notes.title: Structural Analysis (CE3501) • Unit III: Moment Distribution Method (Hardy Cross)
notes.subject: Structural Analysis

content.shortNotes: Stiffness Factor ($k$), Distribution Factor ($DF = k/\sum k$), Carry-Over Factor ($COF = +0.5$ for fixed far end, $0$ for hinged), Analysis of Continuous Beams with Support Settlement, Analysis of Single-Bay Portal Frames with Sway, Symmetrical and Anti-symmetrical Frames.
content.keyPoints:
• Hardy Cross method iteratively relaxes clamped joint moments without simultaneous equations.
• Distribution factors at any rigid joint always sum strictly to 1.0.
• Sinking of supports induces initial fixed-end moments $M_{FAB} = -\frac{6EI\Delta}{L^2}$.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Continuous beam analysis with support settlement using Moment Distribution Method.
2. 16-Mark: Single-bay portal frame sway analysis using Moment Distribution.
3. 2-Mark: Define Distribution Factor and Carry-Over Factor.
content.mcqs: 1. Carry-over factor to a rigidly fixed far end in Moment Distribution is: A) +0.5 [CORRECT] B) 0 C) -0.5
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is Stiffness Factor? Ans: Moment required to produce unit rotation at specified joint ($4EI/L$ for fixed far end, $3EI/L$ for hinged far end).
content.summary: Hardy Cross iterative moment distribution, carry-over factors, and sway analysis.

notes.title: Structural Analysis (CE3501) • Unit IV: Flexibility Matrix Method
notes.subject: Structural Analysis

content.shortNotes: Static Indeterminacy ($D_s$), Flexibility Coefficients ($f_{ij}$), Compatibility Equations, Flexibility Matrix Formulation for Continuous Beams, Pin-Jointed Plane Trusses, and Rigid Frames, Effect of Temperature Changes and Support Sinking.
content.keyPoints:
• Flexibility matrix method treats redundant forces as primary unknowns.
• Flexibility coefficient $f_{ij}$ is displacement at $i$ due to unit force at $j$.
• Flexibility matrix $[F]$ is always symmetric and positive definite ($f_{ij} = f_{ji}$).

2. 16-Mark: Pin-jointed indeterminate truss analysis using Flexibility Matrix.

content.mcqs: 1. Flexibility matrix $[F]$ is the inverse of the: A) Stiffness Matrix $[K]$ [CORRECT] B) Load Vector
content.vivaQuestions: Q: What is the difference between Flexibility and Stiffness methods? Ans: Flexibility uses forces as unknowns with compatibility equations; Stiffness uses displacements as unknowns with equilibrium equations.
content.summary: Flexibility (Force) Matrix method, compatibility equations, and redundant force analysis.

notes.title: Structural Analysis (CE3501) • Unit V: Stiffness Matrix Method & Influence Lines
notes.subject: Structural Analysis

content.shortNotes: Kinematic Indeterminacy ($D_k$), Member Stiffness Matrices, Global Stiffness Matrix $[K]$ Assembly, Analysis of Continuous Beams and Frames, Influence Line Diagrams (ILD) for Determinate and Indeterminate Beams, Muller-Breslau Principle.
content.keyPoints:
• Direct stiffness method forms foundation of modern structural FEM software (STAAD.Pro, ETABS).
• Global system equation: $\{P\} = [K] \{\Delta\}$.
• Muller-Breslau principle: Deflected shape under unit release represents the influence line diagram.

2. 16-Mark: Muller-Breslau Principle for constructing ILD for bending moment and shear force in indeterminate beams.
3. 2-Mark: State Muller-Breslau Principle.
content.mcqs: 1. Direct stiffness method solves structural equations using: A) $\{P\} = [K]\{\Delta\}$ [CORRECT] B) $\{\Delta\} = [K]\{P\}$
content.vivaQuestions: Q: State Muller-Breslau Principle. Ans: The influence line for any internal stress function is given by the deflected shape of the structure when the restraint corresponding to that function is removed and replaced by a unit displacement.
content.summary: Direct stiffness matrix formulation, global stiffness assembly, and Muller-Breslau ILD.

notes.subject: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering

notes.title: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering (IT3401) • Unit II: Client-Side Scripting & Modern JavaScript (ES6+)
notes.subject: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering

content.shortNotes: JavaScript Engine Architecture (V8, Call Stack, Event Loop, Task Queue, Microtask Queue), ES6+ Features (Arrow functions, Destructuring, Promises, async/await, Modules import/export), DOM Manipulation, Event Handling & Bubbling/Capturing, Fetch API, AJAX, Web Storage (localStorage vs sessionStorage).

notes.title: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering (IT3401) • Unit III: Server-Side Scripting & Node.js / Express Backend
notes.subject: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering

content.shortNotes: Node.js Architecture (Non-blocking I/O, Libuv thread pool), NPM Package Management, Express.js Framework (Routing, Middleware pipeline, Error handling), RESTful API Design Principles (Idempotency, Status codes), Authentication & Authorization using JWT (JSON Web Tokens) & bcrypt password hashing.

notes.title: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering (IT3401) • Unit IV: Frontend Frameworks & Component State Management
notes.subject: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering

notes.subject: Web Essentials & Full Stack Engineering

notes.title: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering (BT3451) • Unit I: DNA Structure, Replication & Repair Mechanisms
notes.subject: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering

notes.title: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering (BT3451) • Unit II: Transcription & Post-Transcriptional Processing
notes.subject: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering

content.shortNotes: Prokaryotic Transcription (RNA Polymerase holoenzyme, Sigma factor $\sigma^{70}$, Promoters -10 Pribnow and -35 boxes), Rho-dependent and Rho-independent Termination, Eukaryotic Transcription (RNA Polymerase I, II, III, TATA Box, Transcription Factors TFIID), Post-Transcriptional Modifications (5' 7-methylguanosine Capping, 3' Polyadenylation, Spliceosome-mediated Intron Splicing, Alternative Splicing).
content.keyPoints:
• Sigma factor confers promoter recognition specificity to prokaryotic core RNA polymerase.
• 5' Cap and 3' Poly(A) tail protect eukaryotic mRNA from exonuclease degradation and assist ribosome export.
• Alternative splicing allows a single gene to encode multiple distinct functional protein isoforms.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Mechanism of Transcription initiation, elongation, and termination in prokaryotes.
2. 16-Mark: Post-transcriptional mRNA processing in eukaryotes (Capping, Polyadenylation, Spliceosome Splicing).
3. 2-Mark: What is the role of the Sigma ($\sigma$) factor in transcription?
content.mcqs:
1. Which eukaryotic RNA Polymerase is responsible for synthesizing protein-coding pre-mRNA transcripts?
   A) RNA Polymerase II [CORRECT]
   B) RNA Polymerase I
   C) RNA Polymerase III
   D) Primase
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is Alternative Splicing?
Ans: A regulated post-transcriptional process where exons are included or excluded in different combinations to produce multiple protein variants from one pre-mRNA.
content.summary: Unit II explores RNA synthesis machinery, promoter regulation, spliceosome biochemistry, and mRNA maturation.

notes.title: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering (BT3451) • Unit III: Genetic Code & Translation Mechanism
notes.subject: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering

content.shortNotes: Genetic Code Characteristics (Triplet, Non-overlapping, Degenerate, Universal, Wobble Hypothesis), Ribosome Structure (70S prokaryotic vs 80S eukaryotic), Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetases, Translation Stages (Initiation: Shine-Dalgarno sequence / Kozak consensus, Elongation: EF-Tu, EF-G, Peptidyl Transferase center, Termination: Release Factors RF1/RF2/RF3), Post-Translational Modifications (Phosphorylation, Glycosylation, Proteolytic cleavage).
content.keyPoints:
• Wobble hypothesis allows non-standard base pairing at the 3rd codon position (Inosine with A, U, C).
• Peptidyl transferase is a ribozyme (23S rRNA in prokaryotes) that catalyzes peptide bond formation.
• Shine-Dalgarno sequence binds 16S rRNA to align the bacterial ribosome at the AUG start codon.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Step-by-step mechanism of Translation (Initiation, Elongation, Termination) with ribosome A, P, E site diagram.
2. 16-Mark: Genetic code properties and the Wobble Hypothesis explanation.
3. 2-Mark: State the function of Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase.
content.mcqs:
1. What is the start codon that initiates translation in universal genetic code?
   A) AUG (Methionine) [CORRECT]
   B) UAA
   C) UGA
   D) UAG
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is the Wobble Hypothesis proposed by Francis Crick?
Ans: It states that base pairing between the 3rd nucleotide of the mRNA codon and the 1st nucleotide of the tRNA anticodon is flexible, allowing fewer tRNAs to decode all 61 sense codons.
content.summary: Unit III covers the triplet genetic code, ribosome translation cycles, wobble pairing, and protein folding modifications.

notes.title: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering (BT3451) • Unit IV: Recombinant DNA Tools & Cloning Vectors
notes.subject: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering

content.shortNotes: Type II Restriction Endonucleases (Palindromic sequences, sticky vs blunt cuts), DNA Ligase & Alkaline Phosphatase, Cloning Vectors (Plasmids: pBR322, pUC19 with Blue-White $\text{lacZ}$ screening, Bacteriophage $\lambda$, Cosmids, BACs, YACs, Expression Vectors with inducible promoters), Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR: Denaturation, Annealing, Extension, Primer Design, RT-PCR, Quantitative Real-Time qPCR).
content.keyPoints:
• Type II restriction enzymes cut precisely within recognition sites without requiring ATP.
• pUC19 blue-white screening uses insertional inactivation of $\text{lacZ}\alpha$ gene.
• PCR amplifies target DNA exponentially ($2^n$ fold) using heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Construction of pBR322 and pUC19 cloning vectors with Blue-White colony screening mechanism.
2. 16-Mark: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle, reaction components, and Primer Design criteria.
3. 2-Mark: Why is Alkaline Phosphatase used in vector preparation?
content.mcqs:
1. Recombinant colonies containing DNA inserts in pUC19 vectors appear as which color on X-gal plates?
   A) White [CORRECT]
   B) Blue
   C) Yellow
   D) Red
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: Why is Taq DNA Polymerase used in PCR instead of mammalian DNA polymerase?
Ans: Taq polymerase isolated from thermophilic bacterium *Thermus aquaticus* is thermostable and survives repeated $95^\circ\text{C}$ denaturation cycles.
content.summary: Unit IV covers restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, blue-white selection, and PCR thermal amplification.

notes.title: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering (BT3451) • Unit V: Gene Transfer, Transgenic Applications & CRISPR-Cas9
notes.subject: Molecular Biology & Genetic Engineering

content.shortNotes: Transformation Methods (Chemical $\text{CaCl}_2$, Electroporation, Biolistic Particle Gun, *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* Ti plasmid & T-DNA transfer), Transgenic Plants (Bt Cotton, Golden Rice) & Transgenic Animals, Therapeutic Proteins (Recombinant Human Insulin Production in *E. coli*), CRISPR-Cas9 Targeted Genome Editing (Guide RNA, PAM sequence, NHEJ vs HDR repair), Biosafety & Bioethics.
content.keyPoints:
• *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* natural Ti plasmid transfers T-DNA into plant nuclear genomes.
• Recombinant human insulin (Humulin) is synthesized by expressing A and B peptide chains separately in *E. coli* and forming disulfide bonds.
• CRISPR-Cas9 utilizes single guide RNA (sgRNA) and Cas9 endonuclease for precise double-strand DNA cleavage.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Mechanism of *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* Ti-plasmid mediated gene transfer in plants with T-DNA diagram.
2. 16-Mark: Production of Recombinant Human Insulin using genetic engineering techniques in *E. coli*.
3. 16-Mark: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing mechanism with guide RNA and PAM recognition.
4. 2-Mark: What is the function of the PAM sequence in CRISPR-Cas9?
content.mcqs:
1. Which organism's Ti plasmid is widely utilized as a natural vector for plant genetic engineering?
   A) *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* [CORRECT]
   B) *Escherichia coli*
   C) *Bacillus thuringiensis*
   D) *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: How does CRISPR-Cas9 recognize and cleave target DNA sequences?
Ans: The synthetic single guide RNA (sgRNA) pairs with complementary target DNA adjacent to a Protospacer Adjacent Motif (PAM), directing Cas9 endonuclease to introduce a double-strand break.
content.summary: Unit V explores plant/animal transformation, recombinant human insulin bio-manufacturing, and CRISPR gene editing.

notes.title: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (BA3301) • Unit I: Strategic Management Process & Business Vision
notes.subject: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance

content.shortNotes: Strategic Management Framework (Environmental Scanning, Strategy Formulation, Strategy Implementation, Strategy Evaluation), Mission, Vision, Objectives, Core Values, Strategic Intent, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Stakeholder Analysis & Mapping, Balanced Scorecard (Financial, Customer, Internal Business Processes, Learning & Growth Perspectives).
content.keyPoints:
• Vision defines future aspiration; Mission defines current purpose and customer value.
• Balanced Scorecard measures strategic performance across 4 balanced perspectives.
• Stakeholder matrix aligns corporate decisions with power and interest of key constituent groups.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Strategic Management Process phases with feedback loops and decision models.
2. 16-Mark: Balanced Scorecard framework implementation across four operational perspectives.
3. 2-Mark: Differentiate between Vision Statement and Mission Statement.
content.mcqs:
1. Which perspective in the Balanced Scorecard tracks employee training, skills, and corporate culture?
   A) Learning & Growth Perspective [CORRECT]
   B) Financial Perspective
   C) Customer Perspective
   D) Internal Business Process
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is Strategic Intent?
Ans: The long-term strategic direction and ambitious positioning that an organization pursues to achieve market leadership.
content.summary: Unit I covers corporate strategic planning, mission/vision formulation, stakeholder analysis, and Balanced Scorecards.

notes.title: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (BA3301) • Unit II: External Environmental Analysis & Industry Dynamics
notes.subject: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance

content.shortNotes: Macro-Environmental Analysis (PESTEL: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal), Porter's Five Forces Model of Industry Competition (Threat of New Entrants, Buyer Power, Supplier Power, Substitute Threat, Competitive Rivalry), Strategic Group Mapping, Industry Life Cycle (Introduction, Growth, Maturity, Decline), Competitor Intelligence Analysis.
content.keyPoints:
• Porter's Five Forces determines the long-term structural profitability of an industry.
• High entry barriers and high switching costs insulate incumbent firm margins.
• Strategic group mapping reveals direct competitors sharing similar business models within an industry.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: In-depth analysis of Porter's Five Competitive Forces model with tech industry applications.
2. 16-Mark: PESTEL Macro-environmental framework with strategic response matrices.
3. 2-Mark: State the five forces that shape industry competition.
content.mcqs:
1. In Porter's Five Forces, high switching costs for customers lead to:
   A) Decreased Bargaining Power of Buyers [CORRECT]
   B) Increased Threat of New Entrants
   C) Higher Rivalry
   D) Lower Profitability
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What are High Exit Barriers in an industry?
Ans: Specialized assets, emotional commitments, or termination costs that keep unprofitable firms operating, exacerbating price competition.
content.summary: Unit II details PESTEL environmental scanning, Porter's Five Forces industry analysis, and competitor mapping.

notes.title: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (BA3301) • Unit III: Internal Organizational Analysis & Core Competencies
notes.subject: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance

content.shortNotes: Resource-Based View (RBV), VRIO Framework (Valuable, Rare, Inimitable, Organized), Core Competencies & Distinctive Capabilities, Porter's Value Chain Analysis (Primary Activities: Inbound Logistics, Operations, Outbound Logistics, Marketing/Sales, Service; Support Activities: Infrastructure, HR, Tech, Procurement), Benchmarking & SWOT Analysis.
content.keyPoints:
• VRIO framework evaluates whether internal resources deliver sustained competitive advantage.
• Core competencies combine collective learning, coordination of technical skills, and unique culture.
• Value chain analysis identifies cost drivers and differentiation levers across interconnected business activities.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: VRIO framework decision tree and competitive parity vs sustained competitive advantage outcomes.
2. 16-Mark: Porter's Value Chain Analysis (Primary and Secondary support activities) with diagram.
3. 2-Mark: Define Core Competence.
content.mcqs:
1. According to the VRIO framework, a resource that is Valuable, Rare, and Inimitable yields:
   A) Sustained Competitive Advantage [CORRECT]
   B) Competitive Parity
   C) Temporary Advantage
   D) Cost Leadership
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is the difference between Primary and Support activities in Value Chain Analysis?
Ans: Primary activities directly transform inputs into products and deliver them to customers; Support activities provide the infrastructure, technology, and HR needed to sustain primary operations.
content.summary: Unit III explores Resource-Based View (RBV), VRIO competitive testing, and Porter's Value Chain value creation.

notes.title: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (BA3301) • Unit IV: Generic Business Strategies & Corporate Portfolio Matrices
notes.subject: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance

content.shortNotes: Porter's Generic Competitive Strategies (Cost Leadership, Differentiation, Focused Cost, Focused Differentiation), Blue Ocean Strategy vs Red Ocean Strategy, Corporate Portfolio Matrices: BCG Growth-Share Matrix (Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks, Dogs), GE-McKinsey 9-Cell Matrix, Ansoff's Product-Market Growth Matrix (Market Penetration, Market Development, Product Development, Diversification), Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) and Strategic Alliances.
content.keyPoints:
• Cost leadership requires aggressive economies of scale, tight cost control, and standard products.
• Differentiation delivers unique customer value justifying price premiums.
• BCG matrix uses cash generated by 'Cash Cows' to fund high-growth 'Stars' and promising 'Question Marks'.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: Porter's Generic Competitive Strategies with real-world corporate case studies.
2. 16-Mark: BCG Growth-Share Matrix and strategic cash allocation recommendations.
3. 16-Mark: Ansoff Product-Market Growth Matrix strategies (Market Penetration vs Diversification).
4. 2-Mark: What is a Blue Ocean Strategy?
content.mcqs:
1. In the BCG Matrix, business units with high market share in low-growth mature markets are designated as:
   A) Cash Cows [CORRECT]
   B) Stars
   C) Question Marks
   D) Dogs
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is the difference between Related and Unrelated Diversification?
Ans: Related diversification leverages shared technology, distribution, or customers (synergy); Unrelated diversification enters completely different industries primarily for financial portfolio risk reduction.
content.summary: Unit IV covers Porter's competitive strategies, Blue Ocean innovation, BCG growth matrices, and Ansoff growth paths.

notes.title: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance (BA3301) • Unit V: Strategy Implementation, Corporate Governance & Ethics
notes.subject: Strategic Management & Corporate Governance

content.shortNotes: Strategy Implementation Challenges (McKinsey 7S Framework: Strategy, Structure, Systems, Shared Values, Style, Staff, Skills), Organizational Structure Alignment (Functional, Divisional, Matrix, Network), Corporate Governance Principles, Cadbury Committee & OECD Guidelines, Board Composition & Independent Directors, Business Ethics, Whistleblower Policy, ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) Reporting & Sustainable Value Creation.
content.keyPoints:
• Structure follows strategy; matrix and network organizations enhance agility in dynamic markets.
• McKinsey 7S framework aligns hard elements (Strategy, Structure, Systems) with soft elements (Shared Values, Staff, Style, Skills).
• Corporate governance ensures board independence, executive accountability, and shareholder transparency.
content.importantTopics:
1. 16-Mark: McKinsey 7S Framework for strategic alignment and organizational change management.
2. 16-Mark: Corporate Governance principles, Board of Directors oversight, and ESG sustainability reporting.
3. 2-Mark: Name the components of the McKinsey 7S Framework.
content.mcqs:
1. In the McKinsey 7S framework, which element sits at the central connecting core?
   A) Shared Values [CORRECT]
   B) Strategy
   C) Staff
   D) Structure
content.vivaQuestions:
Q: What is the primary role of Independent Directors on a Corporate Board?
Ans: To provide unbiased, objective oversight, protect minority shareholder rights, and prevent executive conflicts of interest.
content.summary: Unit V covers organizational structure alignment, McKinsey 7S change models, and corporate governance compliance.
